numeric_and_order_audit.lowest_id_reason: M348 initializes center ID 0 and replaces the current winner only on strict lower distance; the fresh 3000-entry scoreboard matches center and ID, and the unchanged numeric-core SHA was independently trace-reconstructed in M350.
numeric_and_order_audit.signed_mask_reason: For use_pwp, plus=original&~center and minus=center&~original; for fallback, plus=original and minus=0. Fresh outputs match all 3000 expected entries.
numeric_and_order_audit.wrapper_transparency: M356 directly wires every output from the unchanged M348 core and adds gates only to configuration and input control.

sticky_error_attack_matrix.finding: M356 is a real handshake quarantine, not a mask-only external-active repair. Once core_cfg_protocol_error rises, external cfg_ready/cfg_active/in_ready are low, core-facing cfg_valid/in_valid are low, and neither internal active nor configuration state can revive before reset.

timing_bypass_audit.bad_beat_handshake: The invalid beat is accepted while error is low, as required to detect the violation. The sequential core raises sticky error and clears active on that edge.
timing_bypass_audit.post_error_combinational_gate: cfg_ready=core_cfg_ready&&!error; cfg_active=core_cfg_active&&!error; in_ready=core_in_ready&&!error; core cfg_valid and in_valid are independently ANDed with !error.
timing_bypass_audit.stale_output_escape: A configuration error can be accepted only when core cfg_ready is high, and M348 defines cfg_ready as pipeline empty. Therefore an error cannot be injected while accepted numeric outputs remain in flight.

stall_latency_and_ii1.finding: The global advance pipeline holds output valid/payload under backpressure and sustains a long one-input-per-cycle run. This is directed functional II1 evidence, not a synthesized Fmax or throughput/mm2 result.

p2.title: Forty attempts are presentation cycles, not forty accepted legal beats
p2.evidence: After sticky error cfg_ready is low. The shipped probe keeps cfg_valid high but advances cfg_group and payload every cycle instead of holding the first unaccepted beat stable.
p2.impact: The adversarial sweep is useful and all forty cycles are blocked, but standard ready/valid wording should not call them forty legal configuration beats.
p2.required_fix: Rename the counter sticky_reconfiguration_attempt_cycles. Add a compliant master test that holds group0 stable until reset and prove no handshake/state mutation throughout the hold.

p2.title: Receipt handshake zero is derived indirectly
p2.evidence: The runner parses attempts but writes sticky_reconfiguration_handshakes=0 as a constant; the TB guarantees zero by fataling whenever cfg_ready is observed.
p2.impact: The result is correct, but the receipt does not parse an explicit handshake counter.
p2.required_fix: Add and print external/core handshake counters, then parse both into the receipt.

p2.title: Shipped SVA observes only wrapper-facing quarantine
p2.evidence: M356 SVA asserts cfg_ready/cfg_active/in_ready low but does not bind core-facing valids, core active, cfg_next_group or pattern-state stability.
p2.impact: The auxiliary M357 VCS attack closes this review gap, but the production assertion package itself would not detect every mask-only internal repair.
p2.required_fix: Bind internal quarantine assertions or expose a small verification interface before Formality.

p2.title: Reload and reset coverage remains bounded
p2.evidence: M356 covers five partial/error configurations and clean post-reset operation, but not an invalid reload after a previously active catalog, reset mid-pipeline/output-stall, or atomic legal catalog replacement after drain.
p2.impact: This does not reopen the repaired sticky-error counterexample, but it limits protocol-complete integration claims.
p2.required_fix: Add active-catalog bad-reload, mid-pipeline reset and drain-then-reload regressions before using the block in a complete PWP executor.
